title: Working with Objects
objective: Add, modify, and delete properties on an existing object, and define a method that uses this.

sourceAlignment.title: JavaScript Crash Course
sourceAlignment.author: Nick Morgan
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only; this book chapter covers both arrays and objects — Code Forge splits them into separate chapters. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: An object isn't fixed once you create it. Assigning to a new key adds it: recruit.rank = "apprentice"; works even if rank didn't exist a moment ago.

Assigning to a key that already exists overwrites its value — that's how you update an object as things change. The delete keyword removes a key entirely: delete recruit.rank; and afterward reading recruit.rank gives undefined again, as if it were never set.

A method is just a function stored as a property. Inside a method, the special keyword this refers to the object the method was called on, so a method can read and change that object's own properties without needing them passed in as arguments.
explanation.rule: obj.key = value adds or overwrites a property; delete obj.key removes one; this inside a method refers to the object it was called on.

examples.title: Adding, Updating, Deleting
examples.note: The property is added, then overwritten, then removed entirely — the final read gives undefined.

examples.title: A Method Using this
examples.note: this.count inside increment() refers to counter's own count property, so each call updates the same object.

checks.question: Inside a method, what does this refer to?
options: The object the method was called on
Nothing — this isn't valid inside a method

feedback.correct: Correct — this refers to whichever object the method was called on.
feedback.incorrect: this refers to the object the method is called on, e.g. counter.increment() means this is counter inside that call.

assignment.title: Durability Tracker
assignment.brief: Write repair(amount) that builds an item object starting at { durability: 50 } with a repairBy(amt) method that adds amt to durability using this, calls that method with amount, then logs the updated durability.
requirements: Build an item object with durability: 50 and a repairBy(amt) method using this.durability.

hints: Create the item object with durability: 50 first.
Give it a method, e.g. repairBy(amt) { this.durability += amt; }.
Call item.repairBy(amount) to apply the change.
50 + 15 is 65 — that's what item.durability should read afterward.
